title: John Lennon receives Green Card for permanent US residency | 1976
content:
John Lennon was awarded permanent residence in the United States on 27 July 1976.

He and Yoko Ono attended a 90-minute hearing at the Immigration and Naturalization Services building in New York City at 1pm. After being sworn in, Lennon was asked a series of routine questions by his lawyer, Leon Wildes, after which he was given the opportunity to make a statement about his desire to achieve permanent resirence.

I’d like to publicly thank Yoko, my wife, for looking after me and holding me together for four years, and giving birth to our son at the same time. There were many times I wanted to quit and she stopped me. I’d like to also thank the cast of thousands, famous and unknown, who have been helping me publicly and privately for the last four years. And my last but not least thank you, my attorney Leon Wildes for doing a good job, and I hope that this is the end of it.
John Lennon

He was then asked a single question by US government attorney William Dunlop, to which he replied in the negative: “Have you left the
United States at all since you entered on August 13th, 71?”

Wildes also brought in several witnesses to bolster Lennon’s case: ATV president Sam Trust, writer Norman Mailer, broadcaster Geraldo Rivera, sculptor Isamu Noguchi, and actor Gloria Swanson.

Wildes and Dunlop then summarised their cases, with Dunlop stating that the government offered no objection to Lennon becoming a permanent resident of the US. It was then formalised by Judge Ira Fieldsteel.

I find him statutorily, and from the point of view of discretion, eligible for permanent residence. It is ordered that the application for adjustment of status under Section 245 of the Immigration and Nationality Act be granted.
Judge Irea Fieldsteel

Lennon was presented with his coveted Green Card by District Director Maurice Kiley. It allowed him to feely travel in and out of the USA, and gave him permission to apply for full citizenship in 1981.

Afterwards Lennon and Wildes held an impromtu press conference outside the courthouse.

As usual, there’s a great woman behind every idiot, and she’s the one. She kept me together, you know. I would have fallen apart long time ago, and she pulled me through it. And here I am, and I thank her, and God bless her.
John Lennon
